items.answer: Provide the mapping of the Indicator 2 (days with delay) and Indicator 3 (delays in 12 months) dropdown options to Watchlist levels (WL). Success = the contract functions return the specified WL for every option and RangeError otherwise, verified by node --test.
No end users/roles in this slice; consumers are later POC screens/code calling the exported functions. No role-based access applies.
In: REQ-03-02 and REQ-03-03 (option lists + WL mapping functions). Out: Indicator 1 and its collapsing of indicators 2-3, any UI, counting delays.
items.quote: Indicator 1 (repayment delay yes/no) and its collapsing of indicators 2–3 are OUT of scope here.

items.answer: Yes: AC summaries plus C1/C2/C5 give every option's exact WL and the invalid-input rule; BA derives Given/When/Then in PLAN.
items.quote: >3 days → WL=2; >60 days → WL=3; >90 days → WL=4

items.answer: Only apparent difference: the POC writes '≤3 days' while C1 fixes the string as '<=3 days'. Resolved by C1 (the clarification confirmed by the business unit wins); no other contradictions found.
items.quote: Dropdown values are exactly these strings

items.question: Is there a MoSCoW priority between REQ-03-02 and REQ-03-03?
options: Both Must, ship together (assumed; they are independent)
items.impact: None on behaviour; only delivery order. Request says they are independent of each other and worked in parallel.

items.answer: daysWithDelay.mjs: DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS (5 strings in order: 'no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days') and daysWithDelayWl(option)→0|2|3|4. delayCount.mjs: DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS ('0','1','>1') and delayCountWl(option)→0|1|2. Mapping: no delay/<=3 days→0, >3→2, >60→3, >90→4; '0'→0, '1'→1, '>1'→2. Input trimmed with String.prototype.trim(), exact case-sensitive match, inner whitespace untouched.
Any value not in the list after trim (wrong case, inner-space change, empty string, null/undefined, number, other non-string) throws RangeError.
items.quote: Matching is exact and case-sensitive after trimming

items.question: Is the RangeError message text part of the contract (and are the functions allowed to expose the offending value in it)?
options: Message unspecified; tests assert only the RangeError type (recommended)
Fixed message text defined by business
items.impact: Tests may over-constrain if text is fixed; only type is stated.
